Ana (PM): Quick sync — we need to lock the PRD acceptance criteria around inference SLAs for launch. Specifically: latency budgets, error-budget burn policy, and graceful-degrade options. Proposing a concrete set so engineering can scope.

Malik (Eng): +1. We should do route-level SLOs (chat vs embeddings vs rerank). One global SLA causes weird tradeoffs.

Priya (SRE): Draft burn policy idea: short burn = throttling + alert; medium = automatic degrade to cheaper model variant + enable cache; long = circuit-break to read-only cached responses for non-critical routes. Need to decide thresholds. :warning:

Ethan (ML Eng): Important: model fallback may change output quality and break customers. We need a regression eval and a visibility signal in the console showing when degrade happened and which model served.

Sam (Product Ops): For acceptance criteria at launch I want: 1) clear SLO numbers per route, 2) automated alerting with runbook links, 3) degrade UX defined (what customers see), 4) telemetry to compute true cost impact.

Malik (Eng): Proposed SLOs (initial):
```yaml
routes:
  chat:
    p50: 120ms
    p95: 350ms
    p99: 900ms
    availability: 99.7%
  embeddings:
    p50: 80ms
    p95: 200ms
    p99: 600ms
    availability: 99.8%
error_budget_week: 0.25%
```
This is conservative but gives room.

Priya (SRE): I think error_budget_week 0.25% is reasonable. Also define burn rate actions:
- burn < 1% of budget: notify (pager optional)
- 1-10%: auto-throttle + enable degraded model
- >10%: open incident + rollback to cached responses for non-essential endpoints

Ethan (ML Eng): Edge cases to call out in PRD: long-context tokens (latency scales), streaming vs non-streaming paths, batch inference tail latency, and token-limited fallbacks. We should add acceptance tests for each.

Sam (Product Ops): UX degrade options we discussed:
- reduce max_tokens and set a short timeout
- return a cached or placeholder response with a banner: "Temporary performance mode — response may be shorter"
- for embeddings, fall back to cheaper quantized model with explicit flag in response headers

Malik (Eng): Implementation note: routing policy will be a policy chain: prefer primary model -> if capacity: primary; if high latency -> model-variant; if error budget exceeded -> cached. Example config snippet: 
```json
{"policy_chain":["primary","variant-small","cache","503-fallback"]}
```

Priya (SRE): Edge case: what if cached content is stale for time-sensitive customer requests? We need a whitelist of customer routes that never serve cache and instead get prioritized capacity (reduce throttle). Add to PRD.

Ana (PM): Decision items for this thread:
1) Approve per-route SLO numbers (Malik proposal) or adjust.
2) Agree error budget and burn thresholds.
3) Confirm degrade UX options (Sam's list).
4) Owners for acceptance tests and rollout gating.

Malik (Eng): I can own the routing policy and config. ETA: proto + unit tests by next Tue.

Priya (SRE): I'll own burn policy automation + runbooks. Will write runbook PR by Fri.

Ethan (ML Eng): I'll produce regression evals for primary->variant transitions and add canary checks. Need help from QA.

Sam (Product Ops): I'll draft the UX copy for fallback banner and the customer-facing FAQ.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy started for service/inference-runtime:v2 -> canary group 5%

Ana (PM): Great. Last ask: add an explicit acceptance criterion in the PRD that states: "If canary shows >2% increase in regression rate on golden promptset when switching to variant, block rollout." Put that into the PRD and ping this thread.

Priya (SRE): Noted. I'll also add monitoring alerts: regression-rate > 1% -> page, >2% -> block and rollback.

Ana (PM): ✅ Thanks all — I'll update the PRD with owners and the numbers. If anyone has strong objections to the SLO numbers above speak up now, otherwise I'll mark as accepted and create the rollout checklist.

Malik (Eng): No objections from me.

Ethan (ML Eng): OK from ML.

Sam (Product Ops): Fine with me.

Priya (SRE): OK. I'll link the runbook next.

Ana (PM): Action items -> Ana: update PRD, Malik: routing proto, Priya: runbook, Ethan: evals, Sam: UX copy. Target deliverables before next sync: PRD v1 + rollout checklist. :spiral_calendar:
